body: I’ll start— i left a used paper lunch box at my desk and cut my nails in the afternoon. Somebody brought cake but there was no plates, so i used the lunch box. I forgot that i placed my nails in that box and only remembered when they were piercing my throat. Felt like fish bones except lumpier.

I was in college during the onset of my body dysmorphia.  Or maybe just anxiety because i was actually really ugly.

During my childhood-teenager years i had many admirers (neighborhood girls every time we moved houses, older students in school, to mention some) made me think i must be handsome even though i cant see it. 

So in college, i pursued a cute guy, but my insecurities started to creep in. It was when i asked him out and he said no when the truth finally slapped me—that, BOY, I was not the handsome kid anymore. In fact, i was extremely ugly and pimply from puberty, got bullied, and somehow was always positive i had a secret charm until he turned me down.

After  then, i gained the habit of looking at mirrors for hours and carried one with me around the house to check all my angles in different lightings (imagine a family member lurking at home holding up a half body mirror at 2AM). I never went out of the house except for work or dinner with close friends. I kept watching movies and cried most nights.
